**About Kanpla

**Kanpla helps contract catering providers create better dining experiences while reducing food waste. What began as a school project now serves more than 800,000 users across more than 5,000 locations in 14 countries.

With more than $10 million raised and a team of 70+ people, we are growing across Europe and building our presence in the US. A great hardware operation can either helps us scale faster or slow down growth, which is why we are creating this role now.

Who you will work with You will work closely with various departments, and extremely closely with the Executive team. You will partner with Product and Engineering to test, innovate and qualify devices and external products we use, and with Delivery, Sales, and Finance on forecasting, pricing, and launch planning. Externally, you will own our relationships with vendors, distributors, installers, and other key partners.

**About The Role

**Every Kanpla launch depends on physical equipment. POS terminals, kitchen display screens, self-service kiosks, and digital signage must be specified, purchased, stored, configured, shipped, installed, and supported across several countries. When that operation works, customers go live on the date we promised. When it does not, the delay and friction are very visible. As our first Head of Hardware and Partnerships, you will set Kanpla’s hardware strategy and own and be responsible for developing and establishing all key operational partnerships across our markets. You will build a scalable function from signed contract to live site, and give Kanpla a reliable view of demand, stock, cost, and supply risk.

**What You Will Do

**

• Define and own Kanpla’s hardware and partnership strategy together with the Executive team.

• Own, develop, and establish all key operational partnerships across our markets, including vendors, distributors, installers, and field engineers.

• Set Kanpla’s recommended hardware range with Product and CS, based on customer needs, reliability, performance, and cost.

• Own hardware commercials, including terms, service levels, pricing, and margins.

• Make sure configured equipment reaches every customer site in time for launch, and build the processes and team to scale it.

• Forecast demand from the pipeline and set the inventory strategy, balancing launch readiness with working capital.

• Identify supply risks early, including single-source dependencies and end-of-life devices, and qualify alternatives before they are needed.

• Own shipping compliance for the UK and Ireland, the Nordics, DACH, Benelux, and the US, including new markets as we enter them.

**What You Will Bring

**There are different routes into this role. Strong candidates are likely to bring most of the following:

• Substantial experience in hardware operations, supply chain, procurement, or partner management, including in a strategic or leadership role.

• Hands-on experience with POS, payments, kiosk, self-service, digital signage, or closely related customer-site hardware. This is essential.

• A record of building strategic partnerships and negotiating commercial agreements.

• Practical knowledge of cross-border shipping, customs, duties, and Incoterms across multiple European markets.

• Technical confidence to assess specifications, and the commercial sense to link hardware decisions to margins and growth.

• Clear communication, comfort working with executives, and experience building teams.

• Fluent English and based in the EU

**What We Offer

**

• Ownership of a function that directly affects every customer launch and our expansion.

• The opportunity to shape Kanpla’s hardware and partnership strategy and build a team.

• Close collaboration with the Executive team and leaders across the company.

• A product that helps improve dining experiences.

• Competitive salary based on experience and real support for your professional growth.

• Remote-first working and two company off-sites or workcations each year.

**Practical details

**The role is remote and EU based, covering the UK and Ireland, the Nordics, DACH, Benelux, and our growing US business. Expect regular travel to partners and occasional customer-site visits.

About the Office of AI

The Office of AI owns the strategy, governance, infrastructure, and enablement of AI across Usercentrics. We sit within the CTO office and work across all departments.

Mission: enable the entire organisation to adopt AI safely, responsibly, and effectively.

About the role

You are the senior technical owner of AI enablement at Usercentrics: the person who takes the hardest department AI builds, the deepest platform problems, and the technical bar the rest of the enablement track works to.

The role has two layers, and we mean both. At the department layer, you do what every AI Enablement Engineer does, prototyping and shipping AI applications for Finance, Legal, HR, Marketing, Customer Success, BI and beyond, but you take the hardest ones yourself and set the pattern the others follow. At the platform layer, you own the infrastructure that makes all of that possible: the LLM access gateway, RAG infrastructure, model operations, evaluation frameworks, and the engineering standards product teams build against.

What you would be walking into: a real internal AI platform already adopted across the company, the AI Hub, MCP servers, Claude connector delivery, a skill hub, usage analytics, and low-code automation. The next layer is largely open. A gateway, RAG infrastructure, model operations, and evaluation frameworks are the current candidates, and you would have a strong say in what gets built and in what order. Real adoption already exists, which is a rarer starting point than a blank slate.

The role asks for two things at once. You are a deeply technical engineer who can architect and build these systems hands-on, at the hardest end of the department builds and the platform layer both. And you build a technical community: you raise the bar across the Enablement Engineers and beyond through education, mentoring, and reusable patterns. If you only have one of these, this is probably not your role.

You will work alongside the AI Enablement Lead, who owns the non-technical adoption pillar (the champion network, AI literacy, and the cross-department use-case pipeline). Your focus is the engineering depth behind that pipeline, from the department app someone is using tomorrow to the platform layer that will still be standing in two years.

On the shape of it: this is a small, senior team today, four to five people, and growing on both the engineering and enablement sides. You would be the most senior engineer on the enablement track and the technical bar would be yours to set.

Requirements

What you will do

• Take on the hardest department AI application builds yourself, and set the technical pattern the AI Enablement Engineers work to

• Own the platform layer that supports every department build: LLM access gateway, RAG infrastructure, model operations, and evaluation frameworks are the current candidates, and you help decide what they are

• Own the internal AI marketplace: keep the cross-departmental AI apps secure, maintained, and governed as the number of them grows

• Own evaluation frameworks and the guardrails that let the team move fast without shipping unreliable AI: output quality, hallucination detection, regression testing

• Set the engineering standards and integration patterns for AI that product and department teams build against

• Raise the engineering bar across the org. Run technical education and enablement for engineers, document reusable patterns, and mentor builders beyond your own team

• Partner with the AI Enablement Lead, Security, and Platform Engineering to ship AI capabilities that are safe, governed, and adopted

• Translate company-wide AI goals into concrete engineering roadmaps and measurable outcomes

What you bring

• 8+ years in software engineering, with significant time at staff level owning complex systems end to end

• Staff-level technical depth. You can own the most complex problems on the enablement track, from a department build to platform infrastructure, and lead by being the strongest engineer in the room

• Genuinely hands-on with AI. You have built and shipped production systems with LLMs, AI agents, RAG, or applied ML yourself, at both application and infrastructure layers

• A strong engineering foundation in distributed systems, backend platform design, and cloud architecture (Azure or GCP), with the judgement to set standards others follow

• A track record of mentoring senior engineers and unblocking ambiguous architecture without heavy process overhead

• A real technical-community or education background. You have taught, mentored at scale, run developer communities, written the docs, or evangelised technology to engineers beyond your own team

• Clear, direct communication, strong in async and written form. You align stakeholders across security, platform, and product without slowing the team down

Nice to have

• Experience with multi-cloud infrastructure (Azure, GCP) and modern DevOps practices

• Background in AI governance, evaluation, or responsible AI deployment

• Experience operating in a regulated or privacy-focused domain

• Recognition as a developer advocate, community leader, conference speaker, or similar (e.g. Google Developer Expert)

• Former founder or CTO experience, comfortable owning ambiguity end to end

Benefits

• Company culture is important to us. We strive to continuously develop a positive, vibrant and inspiring environment that enables everyone to thrive both personally and professionally

Join OrderYOYO’s Data team to build the data pipelines and lakehouse that power executive reporting and merchant insights across our platform, and automate how we deliver finance data and AI-driven data products to the rest of the business.

You’ll own complex changes from technical design through release and production operation, working closely with the leadership team, Finance, Product and fellow engineers. Your work will improve the accuracy and reliability of our reporting, merchant insights and finance data, while reducing routine manual Finance work.

Our data platform runs in a Microsoft Azure cloud environment, and we’re moving it to Microsoft Fabric. We value transferable experience: strong Azure Databricks or Synapse engineers who can quickly develop deep Fabric expertise are encouraged to apply. This is a hands-on engineering role, not a pure architecture, BI or people-management position, and you’ll regularly design, code, troubleshoot and operate production data solutions.

**Role Mission

**Build and evolve OrderYOYO’s data platform into a single source of truth for executive reporting, merchant insights, finance automation and AI, leading the move to a modern Microsoft Fabric lakehouse. You’ll help strengthen the reliability and quality of our data in production while building AI into how we deliver data products and supporting our growing international restaurant platform.

**Core Responsibilities

**

• Design, build and operate production-grade data solutions in Microsoft Fabric across Lakehouse, Warehouse, notebooks, pipelines and related platform capabilities.

• Build and run production pipelines in Fabric, Python and PySpark that are tested and maintainable, not just notebooks.

• Design ingestion and transformation patterns that scale across multiple source systems, databases and business domains while controlling source impact, concurrency and platform cost.

• Manage Fabric capacity and cost, and retire redundant legacy layers.

• Lead migrations from legacy to modern platforms with metric parity, stakeholder sign-off, change control and safe decommissioning.

• Run the platform in production: monitoring, alerting, incident triage, root-cause analysis, data-quality checks, lineage and runbooks.

• Diagnose and resolve production issues across SQL, Spark, pipelines and semantic models, including performance degradation, data failures and capacity/resource constraints.

• Support and evolve governed semantic models and reusable metric definitions, working closely with analytics and business stakeholders to ensure performance, consistency and reliability.

• Build AI into the platform and our delivery: RAG, Azure OpenAI and agents, with prompt and version management.

• Deliver applied data science such as churn, recommendations, personalisation, fraud or risk models, and show the results.

• Work with executives, Finance, Product and engineering, and judge when to move fast, standardise, automate or hold.

**Must-have Requirements

**

• 8+ years of relevant data experience, including substantial recent hands-on data engineering or data-platform engineering responsibility in production environments.

• Demonstrated ability to independently take a data-engineering problem from requirements and technical design through implementation, production deployment, monitoring and ongoing operation.

• Deep hands-on Microsoft Fabric, or strong Synapse, Databricks or Delta experience with a clear path to Fabric.

• Strong understanding of lakehouse architecture and Delta-based data engineering, including partitioning, schema evolution, file optimisation and performance considerations.

• Expert SQL and T-SQL, including complex modelling and tuning.

• Production-grade Python or PySpark.

• Strong experience designing and implementing incremental data ingestion patterns, including approaches such as CDC, change tracking or watermarks, with reliable merge/upsert, replay and idempotent processing.

• Experience with analytical and semantic data modelling, ideally with Power BI/Fabric semantic models, including performance optimisation, governance and reusable business metrics.

• Working knowledge of Azure platform fundamentals including Azure SQL, ADLS/OneLake, Entra ID, managed identities, RBAC and Key Vault.

• A track record of leading a legacy-to-modern migration.

• Real, hands-on AI engineering beyond out-of-the-box Copilot.

• Concrete data science or ML models you delivered, with results.

**Strong-to-have Experience

**

• Strong Power BI/Fabric experience, including Direct Lake, DAX, semantic model performance tuning, incremental refresh and capacity considerations.

• Infrastructure-as-Code experience with Terraform, Bicep or equivalent tooling.

• Data platform experience in SaaS, marketplace, fintech, payments, e-commerce or multi-region businesses.

jobs.description:
Most companies that do conferencing hand you one slice of it. The desktop app, or the media pipeline, or, maybe, the join flow. Everything else you pass over a wall to another team. Not in this case. One team owns the whole path across the Airtame platform: Airtame 3, Airtame Go, Virtual Airtame, and browser, desktop, and mobile apps that go with them. The bar remains at an effortless experience. Someone walks into a room, and starts sharing. No app to hunt for, no login to chase.

The team is four engineers, and we're hiring their technical and people lead: someone who spends about 60% of time hands-on with the hardest problems, and the rest growing the engineers around them.

**About Airtame

**We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and you'd work from there or remotely from within the EU. We make the hardware and the software that runs on it, so a call you make about the streaming stack ends up in a product bolted to a wall in meeting rooms around the world. The team is small, works across disciplines, and reaches a global market from a small base.

Year one outcomes

Make joining a call one step that works. Today, getting an authenticated meeting started from a room takes too many turns: personal logins, manual entry, a different quirk on every platform. A year from now, starting a scheduled call on Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, or Webex should be something a room just does. Judge it by how often it works on the first try, and how rarely it reaches support.

Take the friction out of screen sharing. The browser path loses first-time users: too many clicks, not enough signposting. You'll own getting a newcomer from a short code to their screen on the wall without a stumble, and getting Miracast and AirPlay stable enough to turn on by default.

Make it behave the same everywhere. The experience varies between Airtame 3, Virtual Airtame, browser, desktop, and mobile today. By year-end, sharing and calling should feel like one product no matter which surface you're on, with real-time quality that holds up on whatever network the room happens to have.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've owned a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped building. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• Comfortable across the stack. Real-time media is second nature to you: WebRTC, streaming, the way audio and video behave over a network you don't control. You've gone deep somewhere, whether a media pipeline, native protocols, or a cross-platform client, and you can hold your own everywhere else, on browser, desktop, and mobile.

• You've made stubborn systems cooperate. Half this job is getting software to play nicely with platforms you don't own: Teams, Zoom, Meet, Webex, the operating system's own media APIs, each with its own idea of how things should go. You've done that kind of integration, and you keep your head when every platform behaves differently.

• You measure yourself by the room. Your bar is the person standing at the "share" button. Someone who's never seen an Airtame, getting their screen up first try with no help. That's what you optimize for, and it steers the calls you make when something has to give.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.

**Logistics

**Location: Remote in Europe, or hybrid from our Copenhagen office.

Employment type: Full-time preferred. We're also open to a project-based contract scoped to delivering the native protocol implementations.

****Why Airtame:

• The defining calls are still ahead. Airtame's collaboration software keeps spreading across more devices and form factors, so the shape of the next phase is still open, and you'd be the one setting it.

• At our size, a major call you make shows up in front of customers within weeks, so the feedback comes back fast.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Significant responsibility and ownership over projects and your field of expertise.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

****What Our Employment Decisions Are NOT Based On

****Race, colour, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, disability, ethnicity, national origin, marital status, family or parental status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other legally protected classification or status. And we will not tolerate discrimination or harassment.

****What Our Employment Decisions ARE Based On

****Business needs, job requirements, individual qualifications, and candidates potential for growing with Airtame.

****How We Handle Your Application Data

****Airtame ApS (CVR 35478973, Copenhagen), together with Airtame US Inc. for US roles, processes the information you submit to assess your application. We do this under the EU General Data Protection Regulation, wherever you are based. Your data is stored in Greenhouse, our recruiting system, which may store it outside the EU under standard EU safeguards. Only the people involved in hiring can see it. For roles with privileged access to our systems, we’ll contact one professional reference or previous employer that you name, to confirm your role and dates. We’ll tell you before we do. We keep your data for 6 months after the recruitment process ends, or longer where US law requires it or where you consent to us keeping it for future roles. To get a copy of your data, correct or delete it, or object to how we use it, write to data@airtame.com. You can also complain to the Danish Data Protection Agency (Datatilsynet).

Job Description

Are you passionate about understanding how offshore wind turbines respond to the forces of nature? Do you want to use your engineering expertise to influence the design, performance and long-term reliability of offshore wind farms?

At Vattenfall, we believe there is a way to build a more sustainable energy future. We're looking for a Senior Offshore Wind Turbine Loads & Structural Dynamics Engineer to join our Structural Loads team within Offshore Engineering.

In this specialist role, you'll work at the heart of offshore wind turbine engineering, using engineering analysis, aeroelastic modelling and measurement data to investigate complex turbine behaviour and turn the results into sound engineering decisions.

From early development and turbine selection through to operational optimisation and lifetime extension, your expertise will help shape important technical decisions across our offshore wind portfolio.

You'll join an international team of engineering specialists who value collaboration, technical excellence and finding practical solutions to complex challenges.

Your Role

As a Senior Offshore Wind Turbine Loads & Structural Dynamics Engineer, you'll combine hands-on technical expertise with responsibility for delivering complex engineering work across offshore wind projects and operating assets.

Working closely with multidisciplinary engineering teams, turbine manufacturers and external partners, you'll help ensure our offshore wind turbines are designed and operated safely, efficiently and reliably.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Advanced engineering analysis: Independently define, perform and technically own aeroelastic load analyses, including modelling strategy, execution, validation and interpretation, turning complex results into sound engineering conclusions and decisions.

• Structural integrity: Assess wind turbine and support-structure loading and independently investigate and resolve complex engineering questions relating to fatigue, structural performance and lifetime extension.

• Project delivery: Technically lead load-related engineering activities, ensuring technical deliverables meet project requirements, quality standards and deadlines, and act as the Structural Loads technical point of contact for assigned projects.

• Technical collaboration: Work closely with specialists across Wind Turbine Engineering, Primary Structures, Geotechnical Engineering and Metocean to solve multidisciplinary engineering problems where turbine loads, structural response and environmental conditions interact.

• Stakeholder engagement: Act as a trusted technical partner to internal stakeholders, understanding their needs and translating complex loads-related questions, risks and results into clear engineering recommendations that support project decisions.

• Innovation and improvement: Develop and refine simulation models, engineering tools and analysis methods to improve turbine performance, reduce technical risks and support continuous improvement.

Your Profile

We're looking for an experienced engineering specialist who can independently investigate and solve complex engineering problems, translating detailed analysis into well-founded engineering conclusions and practical solutions.

You'll bring a strong understanding of wind turbine aeroelasticity and structural dynamics, alongside the ability to take technical ownership, exercise sound engineering judgement and communicate complex technical matters clearly and effectively across different disciplines.

Qualifications

• A master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Wind Energy or a closely related discipline.

• At least 7 years of relevant industry experience in wind turbine aeroelasticity, load simulation or structural dynamics.

• Extensive hands-on experience defining and performing aeroelastic load analyses, including model development, simulation, validation, post-processing and interpretation of results.

• Strong knowledge of wind turbine aerodynamics, structural dynamics, control systems and load-generation mechanisms.

• Experience interpreting simulation results, validating engineering models and working with measurement data.

• Experience working within multidisciplinary engineering environments, ideally within offshore wind, turbine manufacturing or renewable energy development.

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical findings and collaborate effectively with internal and external stakeholders.

• Professional proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

It would also be beneficial if you have experience in:

• Offshore wind turbine foundation design, hydrodynamics or coupled turbine-foundation analysis.

• Relevant IEC and DNV standards and certification processes.

• Engineering programming tools such as Python or MATLAB.

• Operational load assessments, turbine power upgrades or lifetime extension projects.

Above all, you'll bring curiosity, a careful and structured approach to engineering challenges, and a genuine interest in sharing knowledge and developing solutions together.

Good remuneration, a challenging and international work environment, and the possibility to work with some of the best in the field. You will be working in interdisciplinary teams and you can always count on support from committed colleagues. We offer attractive employment conditions and opportunities for personal and professional development.

jobs.description:
Would you like to build strong and equitable partnerships with Oxfam country offices and partners around the world – and thereby contribute to a fairer world? Then read on!

Who are you?

Oxfam Denmark is strengthening its partnership-centred approach to international development, and we are looking for a Partnership Manager who combines strong relationship skills with solid experience in grant management. We imagine that you have worked with international development and/or humanitarian programmes in an NGO or a similar organisation, and that you have experience within conflict sensitivity and peacebuilding aspects of international programmes. In addition, we are looking for someone who:

• has experience managing grants and projects through their full lifecycle, including donor relations and reporting

• builds trusting partnership relations and is comfortable representing an organisation in international forums

• sees influencing as an integral part of good programming

• is committed to feminist, rights-based, and decolonial principles as embedded in Oxfam Denmark's Local Leadership Strategy

• has a relevant academic degree and speaks and writes fluent English, which is our work language. Proficiency in other languages – French, Arabic, Spanish – is an advantage.

Who are we, and what will you be doing?

Oxfam is one of the world’s largest development and humanitarian organisations, and our analyses and messages are heard by global leaders and in the Danish debate. Together with Oxfam country offices, regional platforms and partner organisations, we work to fight poverty and inequality – and we believe that strong, equitable partnerships are key to lasting change.

You will join the Business Development and Partnerships team in our International Programme Department as one of several Partnership Managers, each carrying a country/regional portfolio together with a thematic focal point role. Your tasks will include:

• managing a portfolio of country and/or regional partner relationships and representing Oxfam Denmark in relevant Oxfam International forums, e.g. the Country Strategy Forum

• overseeing the full lifecycle of assigned grants and projects and supporting donor relations, ensuring timely and high-quality reporting

• ensuring that influencing strategies are integral to project and partnership design

• acting as a focal point for conflict sensitivity and peacebuilding and bringing your expertise into play across the entire portfolio and in support of devolving this capacity into the Global South

Read more in Oxfam Denmark’s strategy here and see the full function description on this page.

What we offer

This is a fixed term position for ending on 01 July 2027, with possibility of extension. Salary and pension according to the applicable in-house agreement. As a non-profit organisation, Oxfam Denmark does not offer top-of-the-market salaries, but you will become part of an organisation with dedicated colleagues who work purposefully to reduce poverty and inequality in an informal working environment.

In addition, we offer:

• Weekly working hours: 37 hours including lunch break. We have flexible working hours including the opportunity to work from home 1-2 days a week.

• The workplace is in the civil society house VOX in newly renovated premises with a lively atmosphere at Lyngbyvej 100, Copenhagen Østerbro – right next to Ryparken Station. Our Copenhagen staff is appx. 70 people.

• We support a lunch scheme in the shared VOX canteen, where the food is predominantly vegetarian.

The practical details

Send us your CV and a cover letter with some thoughts on how you would approach the tasks and how your experience can make a difference for us. Apply via the “Apply” button no later than 15 November 2026. We hope you can start as soon as possible. Interviews are scheduled for 20 November 2026.

You are very welcome to contact Pia Dyrhagen, Teamleader, Programme Quality & Institutional Funding, by email at pdy@oxfam.dk or phone +45 40 13 21 06 to learn more about the position.

We encourage all qualified applicants to apply – regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion or age.

This is a role based in Copenhagen, and you must be eligible to work in Denmark.

About Oxfam Denmark

Oxfam Denmark is an independent and member-based development and humanitarian organisation. We have the world's best cause and high ambitions. Through education, support to civil society and in collaboration with our partners, we fight inequality and poverty in the Global South. Together with 20+ other organisations, we form the Oxfam International confederation, one of the world's largest and most influential development organisations. In Denmark, we are a clear and significant player in the public debate on issues such as tax havens, rising inequality, climate change and the right to education.

You can read more about Oxfam Denmark at About Oxfam.
